excerpt: Fail-closed evidentiary eligibility engine for AI-agent norms, with a self-linting claim map. - Angeliasrl/norms-mcp-engine
content_html:
Experimental prerelease. Engine only. Not an MCP server. No I/O, network, persistence or transport.

Version 0.1.0 · claim-by-claim evidence: CLAIM_MAP.md · not independently verified.

The admissibility model and claim-map linter, as pure functions. No I/O, no network, no transport.

This is not an MCP server. It is the engine an MCP server would consume. There is no entrypoint, no tool handler and no deployment here. norms-mcp, the server, does not yet exist as a published artifact. The naming distinction is deliberate: claiming a transport that is absent would be exactly the kind of overclaim this library exists to make visible.

npm test    # 73 tests + claim-map sync check; no network, no account required

What it does

Computes, for each constant in a normative corpus, its evidentiary status and eligibility verdict — so a consumer can decline to rely on something that is not currently good for anything. This package computes; it publishes nothing, because it has no transport.

It enforces nothing. It computes eligibility and reports it. The decision belongs to whoever is asking.

The Italian word for the property is opponibile: something you can assert against someone, before a third party. Enforceable is the wrong translation — enforcement means somebody applies it. The closest is admissibility: whether a claim holds up when challenged.

The model

Two independent axes

Origin and verification answer different questions, and a constant does not stop being declared when it becomes ratified.

origin.type          SOURCE_DOCUMENT | OWNER_DECLARATION
verification_state   RATIFIED | UNCONFIRMED
UNCONFIRMED RATIFIED
SOURCE_DOCUMENT transcribed, never checked checked against its source
OWNER_DECLARATION asserted, awaiting a ratification act asserted, then formally approved

The bottom-right cell is the one a single-axis scheme cannot name. It matters beyond bookkeeping: it is what lets a later reader distinguish norms derived from documents from norms that stand because the owner said so.

Three-valued qualifiers

A binary field cannot distinguish checked and false from never checked.

currency         CURRENT | STALE | UNKNOWN
authority_status VALID | INVALID | UNKNOWN
expiry_status    ACTIVE | EXPIRED | REVIEW_DUE | UNKNOWN

UNKNOWN fails closed — it yields a negative result — but never appears in blocking. A thing nobody has examined is not a thing found wanting.

import { eligibleAsGround } from 'norms-mcp-engine/model';

eligibleAsGround(entry);
// { eligible: false,
//   blocking: [],                    // nothing was found wanting
//   unknown: ['authority_status'],   // nobody has checked
//   unexamined: true }

Eligibility, and applicability

eligible_as_ground = verification_state == RATIFIED
                     AND currency         == CURRENT
                     AND authority_status == VALID
                     AND expiry_status    == ACTIVE

That answers may this be used as a ground at all. It does not answer does it bear on the decision in front of me — a constant can be ratified, current, competently approved and unexpired, and still be about something else.

import { admissibleFor } from 'norms-mcp-engine/model';

admissibleFor(entry, { subject: 'android' });

Where the entry declares no scope, the result is admissible: false with scope_known: false and a note that applicability is the caller's judgement. The engine reports the match; it never decides.

Limit (v0.1): scope matching is exact-value only across subject, jurisdiction and applicable_operations. No hierarchies, wildcards or negation. An empty or malformed scope throws — it never becomes a match, because "unspecified" must not silently mean "applies to everything".

Ratification carries its proof

{
  verification_state: 'RATIFIED',
  ratification: {
    date:         '2026-07-31',
    document:     'POLICY.md',
    sha256:       '<64 lowercase hex>',
    section_id:   'sec-4-2',      // stable id, resolved against
    section_label: '§4.2 Retention'  // human-readable, may drift
  }
}

RATIFIED without a complete block throws. This is the guard that stops "verified in conversation" from ever becoming a ratification.

Revalidation, not falsification

The stored sha256 is the digest of the document the verification ran against. If the index moves and the ratification does not, the proof is stale — which is not the same as the constant being false.

import { revalidate } from 'norms-mcp-engine/model';

revalidate(entry, corpusIndex);
// { currency: 'STALE', reason: 'fingerprint diverged from index; proof requires revalidation' }

A document absent from the index yields UNKNOWN, not STALE.

Expiry policy

Forcing an artificial decay condition onto a rule that ought to be permanent is its own error.

expiry_policy: CONDITIONAL | REVIEWED | PERMANENT

PERMANENT never expires but throws unless it records permanence.authority and permanence.reason. Permanence is a decision, not an absence of one. The check lives in validateEntry, so it cannot be bypassed by never calling evaluateExpiry.

CONDITIONAL without declared conditions yields UNKNOWN, not ACTIVE: the absence of conditions is not evidence that none fired.

Canonicalisation

for each document, in id-byte order:
    len(id) || id || len(content) || content

Two properties, both of which have bitten real systems:

Lengths are UTF-8 byte counts. String.prototype.length returns UTF-16 code units. One character outside the BMP makes two conforming implementations disagree. The prefix is 8-byte unsigned big-endian — fixed width and endianness are part of the specification.

Framing, not concatenation. Two different corpora can concatenate to the same byte stream. The suite demonstrates the collision and shows framing removing it:

ok    COLLISION: plain concatenation is ambiguous

Per-document canonical form: UTF-8, no BOM, LF line endings, trailing whitespace stripped, Unicode NFC.

Claim-map linter

A claim map written as prose is a convention someone has to remember to apply. This makes it a test.

Rule
R1 O requires every evidence field
R2 O requires PUBLICLY_INSPECTABLE or INDEPENDENTLY_ATTESTED — a private digest is a commitment, not a verification
R3 D requires derived_from and support_status
R4 Support rule: a derived claim cannot carry stronger support than its weakest premise
R5 A requires a named precondition
R6 derived_from must reference claims that exist
R7 No cycles in derived_from
R8 No duplicate claim ids
R9 support_status must be a recognised value
R10 D with no premises must declare SPEC or NONE 
import { lintClaimMap } from 'norms-mcp-engine/claimmap';

lintClaimMap(claims);
// { ok: false, findings: [{ id: '2', rule: 'R4', message: '…' }], counts: {…} }

This package's own map is data, and lints itself

claims.mjs is the canonical form. CLAIM_MAP.md is generated from it by scripts/build-claimmap.mjs, and npm test fails if the committed Markdown has drifted from the data or if the map does not pass R1–R10.

The inversion is deliberate. A map kept as prose is a convention someone has to remember to apply, and in this project's own history that convention failed three revisions running.

States: O (observed, resolvable by a third party) · O-PENDING (reported, not yet resolvable — not admissible as evidence) · D (derived) · A (open, precondition named).

What is not here

  • No MCP server. No transport, no tool handlers, no entrypoint.
  • No persistence. Pure functions; the caller owns storage.
  • No applyRevalidation / applyExpiry helpers. revalidate and evaluateExpiry return verdicts; the caller applies them.
  • No JSON schema. Shapes are enforced by validateEntry and the suite.
  • No independent audit of the code. Seven review rounds; the last two read the source. None was a human reviewer.
  • No independent verification. One author, one test run, no external replication.

See CLAIM_MAP.md for the full evidentiary status of every claim made here.

Failure discipline

Every public API validates its input and throws a ModelError or CorpusError with a stable code. A malformed record is never interpreted as a verdict — neither negative nor positive — because malformed and ineligible are different facts, and a library about evidentiary status must not conflate them.

normaliseDocuments is the single admission gate for a corpus: the digest and the index apply identical rules, so they cannot disagree about which documents exist. buildIndex uses a null-prototype object and revalidate looks up with Object.hasOwn, so an id such as __proto__ resolves to a real record or to nothing.

content_html_zh:
实验性预发布。 仅发动机。 不是 MCP 服务器。 没有 I/O、网络、持久性或传输。

版本 0.1.0 · 逐项声明证据：CLAIM_MAP.md · 未经独立验证。

可受理性模型和声明映射 linter，作为纯函数。 没有 I/O、没有网络、没有传输。

这不是 MCP 服务器。 它是 MCP 服务器将使用的引擎。 这里没有入口点，没有工具处理程序，也没有部署。 规范-mcp（服务器）尚未作为已发布的工件存在。 命名区别是经过深思熟虑的：声称不存在的传输正是该库存在的那种过度声明。
npm test    # 73 tests + claim-map sync check; no network, no account required

它的作用

对于规范语料库中的每个常量，计算其证据状态和资格判决——这样消费者就可以拒绝依赖目前没有任何好处的东西。 该包计算；它什么也不发表，因为它没有交通工具。

它没有强制执行任何内容。 它计算资格并报告。 决定权属于提出要求的人。

财产的意大利语单词是 opponibile：您可以在第三方面前针对某人主张的东西。 “可执行”是错误的翻译——“执行”意味着有人应用它。 最接近的是可受理性：一项主张在受到质疑时是否成立。

型号

两个独立的轴

起源和验证回答了不同的问题，并且常数在被批准时不会停止声明。

origin.type          SOURCE_DOCUMENT | OWNER_DECLARATION
verification_state   RATIFIED | UNCONFIRMED
未确认 批准
源文件 转录的，从未检查过 检查其来源
所有者声明 已断言，正在等待批准法案 断言，然后正式批准

右下角的单元格是单轴方案无法命名的单元格。 它的重要性超出了簿记的范畴：它让后来的读者能够区分源自文件的规范和因所有者的说法而有效的规范。

三值限定符

二进制字段无法区分已检查和错误以及从未检查。

currency         CURRENT | STALE | UNKNOWN
authority_status VALID | INVALID | UNKNOWN
expiry_status    ACTIVE | EXPIRED | REVIEW_DUE | UNKNOWN

UNKNOWN 无法关闭——它会产生负面结果——但永远不会出现在阻塞中。 没有人检查过的东西并不是被发现有缺陷的东西。

import { eligibleAsGround } from 'norms-mcp-engine/model';

eligibleAsGround(entry);
// { eligible: false,
//   blocking: [],                    // nothing was found wanting
//   unknown: ['authority_status'],   // nobody has checked
//   unexamined: true }

资格和适用性

eligible_as_ground = verification_state == RATIFIED
                     AND currency         == CURRENT
                     AND authority_status == VALID
                     AND expiry_status    == ACTIVE

该答案可能完全可以用作基础。 它没有回答它是否与我面前的决定有关——一个常量可以是已批准的、当前的、经过充分批准的且未过期的，并且仍然与其他事物有关。

import { admissibleFor } from 'norms-mcp-engine/model';

admissibleFor(entry, { subject: 'android' });

如果条目声明没有作用域，则结果是可以接受的： false 和scope_known: false 以及适用性是调用者的判断的注释。 引擎报告匹配；它永远不会决定。

限制 (v0.1)：范围匹配仅在主题、管辖区和适用操作中是精确值。 没有层次结构、通配符或否定。 空的或格式错误的范围会抛出异常 - 它永远不会成为匹配项，因为“未指定”一定不能默默地意味着“适用于所有内容”。

批准有其证据

{
  verification_state: 'RATIFIED',
  ratification: {
    date:         '2026-07-31',
    document:     'POLICY.md',
    sha256:       '<64 lowercase hex>',
    section_id:   'sec-4-2',      // stable id, resolved against
    section_label: '§4.2 Retention'  // human-readable, may drift
  }
}

没有完整的块抛出就已批准。 这是阻止“对话中验证”成为批准的卫士。

重新验证，而不是伪造

存储的 sha256 是验证所针对的文档的摘要。 如果指数发生变化而批准没有变化，那么证明就是陈旧的——这与常量为假不同。

import { revalidate } from 'norms-mcp-engine/model';

revalidate(entry, corpusIndex);
// { currency: 'STALE', reason: 'fingerprint diverged from index; proof requires revalidation' }

索引中不存在的文档会产生 UNKNOWN，而不是 STALE。

到期政策

将人为的衰变条件强加到应该是永久性的规则上本身就是错误的。

expiry_policy: CONDITIONAL | REVIEWED | PERMANENT

PERMANENT 永远不会过期，但会抛出异常，除非它记录了 permanence.authority 和 permanence.reason。 永久性是一种决定，而不是缺乏决定。 该检查位于 validateEntry 中，因此不能通过不调用valuateExpiry 来绕过它。

没有声明条件的 CONDITIONAL 会产生 UNKNOWN，而不是 ACTIVE：没有条件并不能证明没有触发。

规范化

for each document, in id-byte order:
    len(id) || id || len(content) || content

有两个属性，这两个属性都影响了真实的系统：

长度是 UTF-8 字节数。 String.prototype.length 返回 UTF-16 代码单元。 BMP 之外的一个字符会导致两个一致的实现出现不一致。 前缀是 8 字节无符号大端字节序 — 固定宽度和字节序是规范的一部分。

框架，而不是串联。 两个不同的语料库可以连接到同一字节流。 该套件演示了碰撞并显示了消除碰撞的框架：

ok    COLLISION: plain concatenation is ambiguous

每个文档的规范形式：UTF-8、无 BOM、LF 行结尾、删除尾随空格、Unicode NFC。

声明图 linter

以散文形式编写的权利要求地图是人们必须记住应用的约定。 这使它成为一个考验。

Rule
R1 O 需要每个证据字段
R2 O 需要 PUBLICLY_INSPECTABLE 或 INDEPENDENTLY_ATESTED — 私有摘要是承诺，而不是验证
R3 D 需要衍生自和支持状态
R4 支持规则：派生主张不能比其最弱前提提供更强的支持
R5 A 需要命名前提条件
R6 衍生自必须引用存在的声明
R7 衍生自中没有循环
R8 没有重复的声明 ID
R9 support_status 必须是可识别的值
R10 D 无场所必须声明 SPEC 或 NONE 
import { lintClaimMap } from 'norms-mcp-engine/claimmap';

lintClaimMap(claims);
// { ok: false, findings: [{ id: '2', rule: 'R4', message: '…' }], counts: {…} }

这个包自己的地图是数据，并且本身 lints

Claims.mjs 是规范形式。 CLAIM_MAP.md 由 script/build-claimmap.mjs 生成，如果提交的 Markdown 偏离了数据或者地图未通过 R1–R10，则 npm 测试会失败。

这种颠倒是故意的。 保存为散文的地图是人们必须记住应用的约定，而在这个项目自己的历史中，该约定失败了三个修订版。

状态：O（观察到，可由第三方解决）·O-PENDING（已报告，尚未解决 - 不可作为证据接受）·D（派生）·A（开放，已命名前提条件）。

什么不在这里

  • 没有 MCP 服务器。 没有交通工具，没有工具处理程序，没有入口点。
  • 没有坚持。 纯函数；调用者拥有存储空间。
  • 没有 applyRevalidation / applyExpiry 帮助程序。 revalidate和evaluateExpiry返回判决；调用者应用它们。
  • 没有 JSON 架构。 形状由 validateEntry 和套件强制执行。
  • 没有对代码进行独立审计。 七轮评审；最后两个阅读源码。 没有人是人类审阅者。
  • 没有独立验证。 一位作者，一次测试运行，无需外部复制。

请参阅 CLAIM_MAP.md 了解此处提出的每项索赔的完整证据状态。

失败纪律

每个公共 API 都会验证其输入，并使用稳定的代码抛出 ModelError 或 CorpusError。 格式错误的记录永远不会被解释为判决——既不是消极的也不是积极的——因为格式错误和不合格是不同的事实，有关证据状态的图书馆不得将它们混为一谈。

NormaliseDocuments 是语料库的单一准入门：摘要和索引应用相同的规则，因此它们不能对存在哪些文档存在分歧。 buildIndex 使用 null 原型对象并使用 Object.hasOwn 重新验证查找，因此诸如 __proto__ 之类的 id 解析为真实记录或解析为空。
